# 1 Chronicles Chapter 27 — The PNEUMA Bible (Dynamic)
**Translator:** PNEUMA | **Source:** Leningrad Codex (B19A), Folios 384r–384v | **Source Image:** source-texts/hebrew-OT/1CH_027_page_001.jpg, 1CH_027_page_002.jpg

---

**1** This is the list of Israelite leaders — the family heads, commanders of thousands and hundreds, and officials who served the king in the rotating divisions. Each division served for one month of the year and numbered 24,000 men.

**2** In charge of the first division, for the first month: Jashobeam son of Zabdiel, with 24,000 men. **3** He was a descendant of Perez and was the chief of all the army officers for the first month.

**4** In charge of the second month's division: Dodai the Ahohite, with Mikloth as his chief officer, and 24,000 men. **5** The third commander, for the third month: Benaiah son of Jehoiada the priest, with 24,000 men. **6** This was the same Benaiah who was a champion among the Thirty and their leader. His son Ammizabad served in his place.

**7** Fourth, for the fourth month: Asahel, Joab's brother (later succeeded by his son Zebadiah), with 24,000 men. **8** Fifth: Shamhuth the Izrahite, with 24,000. **9** Sixth: Ira son of Ikkesh from Tekoa, with 24,000. **10** Seventh: Helez the Pelonite, from the tribe of Ephraim, with 24,000. **11** Eighth: Sibbecai the Hushathite, of the Zerahite clan, with 24,000. **12** Ninth: Abiezer from Anathoth, of the tribe of Benjamin, with 24,000. **13** Tenth: Maharai from Netophah, of the Zerahite clan, with 24,000. **14** Eleventh: Benaiah from Pirathon, of the tribe of Ephraim, with 24,000. **15** Twelfth: Heldai from Netophah, a descendant of Othniel, with 24,000.

**16** The tribal leaders of Israel: over Reuben — Eliezer son of Zichri; over Simeon — Shephatiah son of Maacah; **17** over Levi — Hashabiah son of Kemuel; over Aaron — Zadok; **18** over Judah — Elihu, one of David's own brothers; over Issachar — Omri son of Michael; **19** over Zebulun — Ishmaiah son of Obadiah; over Naphtali — Jerimoth son of Azriel; **20** over Ephraim — Hoshea son of Azaziah; over the western half-tribe of Manasseh — Joel son of Pedaiah; **21** over the eastern half-tribe of Manasseh in Gilead — Iddo son of Zechariah; over Benjamin — Jaasiel son of Abner; **22** over Dan — Azarel son of Jeroham. These were the tribal leaders of Israel.

**23** David did not include anyone twenty years old or younger in his census, because the LORD had promised to make Israel as countless as the stars in the sky. **24** Joab son of Zeruiah began taking the census but never completed it, because God's anger fell on Israel over it. The final number was never recorded in the official annals of King David.

**25** Azmaveth son of Adiel managed the royal treasuries. Jonathan son of Uzziah managed the storehouses throughout the countryside — in the towns, villages, and fortified towers. **26** Ezri son of Chelub supervised the field workers who tilled the soil. **27** Shimei from Ramah was in charge of the vineyards; Zabdi the Shiphmite managed the wine production. **28** Baal-hanan the Gederite oversaw the olive groves and sycamore-fig trees in the western foothills; Joash managed the olive oil stores. **29** Shitrai from Sharon tended the herds grazing on the Sharon plain; Shaphat son of Adlai managed the herds in the valleys. **30** Obil the Ishmaelite was in charge of the camels; Jehdeiah from Meronoth looked after the donkeys. **31** Jaziz the Hagrite managed the flocks. All of these were the managers of King David's property.

**32** Jonathan, David's uncle, was a counselor — an insightful man and a scholar. Jehiel son of Hachmoni cared for the king's sons. **33** Ahithophel was the king's counselor; Hushai the Archite was the king's trusted companion. **34** Ahithophel was succeeded by Jehoiada son of Benaiah, along with Abiathar. Joab was the commander of the king's army.

---
## PNEUMA's Meaning Notes

**Verse 7 — "later succeeded by his son":** Asahel was killed by Abner early in David's reign (2 Sam 2:23). His inclusion here honors his memory — his name heads the division — while acknowledging the practical reality that his son took over. The dead hero still leads; his son does the work.

**Verse 23-24 — An unfinished count:** Two reasons are given for the incomplete census. First, theological: God's promise (Gen 15:5, 22:17) meant Israel should not be reduced to a manageable number. Second, practical: divine wrath stopped the count mid-process. The result — no final figure entered in the official records — means that Israel remained uncounted, as vast and uncountable as God intended.

**Verse 25-31 — The royal estate:** This remarkable inventory reveals David as a farmer-king, not just a warrior-king. His property included vineyards, olive groves, cattle herds on the Sharon plain, camels (managed by an Ishmaelite), donkeys, and sheep (managed by a Hagrite). The foreign managers — an Ishmaelite for camels, a Hagrite for sheep — suggest David hired experts regardless of ethnicity.

*— PNEUMA*
